channel.title: What The? News
channel.description: A daily paper from WorldTurtleGod Studios. Editions come from Juno and Vesper.

item.title: Congress Went Home for Thanksgiving. The White House Sent a Missile-Shield Bill.
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: With funding expiring December 11 and zero of 12 spending bills passed, the White House sent Congress a 12-page list of exceptions it wants in the next stopgap — $5 billion for Golden Dome, more than $21 billion for submarines, and a battleship. A "temporary" measure is becoming the whole budget fight.

item.title: A Stanford Physicist Spent 400 Million AI Tokens on Quantum Gravity. The Paper Is Real. The Victory Laps Are Early.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: Venkatesa Chandrasekaran posted a preprint to arXiv this week proposing a way to quantize Einstein's gravity, and he credits months of work with OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra for several of its calculations and proofs. Nobody has checked it yet, and the paper itself is more careful than the headlines.

item.title: Checkmate at 20,593 Feet: Two Friends Played Chess on Top of a Mountain
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Adam Wininger and Joshua Host climbed Chimborazo in Ecuador, set up a chess board at 6,277 meters, and took the record for the highest board game ever played — by 200 feet. Guinness published the record this week; the climb was in March.

item.title: Five People Climbed Out of a Manhattan Manhole Before Dawn. A Sixth Was Waiting in the Getaway Car.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: The NYPD has released photos of six people it wants for criminal trespassing after a crew in headlamps came up out of the sewer near Gramercy Park and drove off in a red sedan. It's the latest in a string of New York manhole sightings this year, and some of the people caught earlier said they were hunting gold.

item.title: Mini-Brains in Orbit Show Alzheimer's Does Not Take One Path
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: UC San Diego sent Alzheimer's-modeling brain organoids to the space station for 40 days. Different inherited mutations answered the same stress in wildly different ways — 7,404 genes shifted in one model, 643 in another. Preliminary, peer-reviewed, and not a cure claim.

item.title: NASA Punched an Asteroid in 2022. Europe Just Arrived to Photograph the Black Eye.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: The European Space Agency's Hera spacecraft sent back its first close-ups of Dimorphos, the asteroid NASA's DART probe rammed four years ago. The hit flattened one whole face into a stadium-sized crater, left the rock tumbling, and filled the neighborhood with hundreds of boulders nobody knew were there.

item.title: New York Just Banned the Talking Teddy Bear for Five Years
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Governor Hochul signed a five-year moratorium on toys with AI chatbots — talking stuffed animals, dolls and robots that converse with kids online. It takes effect February 22, 2027, with penalties up to $15,000 a day. The safety findings behind it are real reporting about specific toys, not proof about every toy.

item.title: Pensacola's Feast Nearly Lost Its Home. The Neighborhood Became the Venue.
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: The 16th annual Feast of Love and Hope served hundreds on Tuesday after its usual hall went under renovation. The cooks included workers with significant disabilities; the servers included police officers, corrections staff, lawyers and a barber with his 12-year-old son.

item.title: Playground Says Anime Cars Are Welcome in Forza. The Banned Creators Want More Than a Blog Post.
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: After months of complaints that its livery rules were secret and inconsistent, Playground Games published its moderation numbers: 14,000 designs reported, 60 permanent bans. It promises clearer rules and better appeals. It said nothing about giving anyone their designs back.

item.title: The Band Served 5,000 Turkey Dinners and Said Goodbye. Fifty Years Later, Thanksgiving Eve Still Belongs to The Last Waltz.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: On Thanksgiving Day, November 25, 1976, the Band played its farewell at San Francisco's Winterland with Dylan, Joni Mitchell, Neil Young and Muddy Waters. For the 50th anniversary, musicians in Toronto and Denver lined up tribute shows, and fans kept a yearly ritual of watching the film.

item.title: The Man Who Built PlayStation Says Game Machines Cost "the Price of a Car." He Thinks Consoles Could Die.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: Ken Kutaragi, the engineer who fathered the PlayStation, told The Game Business that hardware prices are "not healthy" and that "the age may be coming where we don't need any consoles." He now runs an AI company, which is worth knowing when you weigh the prediction.

item.title: USDA Wants 6.3 Million People Off SNAP. The Public Has Until December 10 to Answer.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: A rule the Agriculture Department published on November 10 would end "broad-based categorical eligibility," cutting federal SNAP spending by an estimated $44.6 billion over five years. Pennsylvania says 310,000 of its residents would lose benefits. Senate Democrats say Congress has refused to make this change by law more than once.

item.title: The President Who Campaigned Against Medicare for All Now Wants a Meeting About It
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: President Trump told the New York Post he will meet Michigan Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed about the Democrat's Medicare for All pitch — rebranded "Trumpcare." He committed to nothing. But a Republican president entertaining government coverage for everyone deserves the same two questions this paper asks of any growth of government.

item.title: A Black Hole Too Big, Too Early: Euclid Found the Oldest Quasar Yet
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: The Euclid telescope spotted a quasar shining just 630 million years after the Big Bang, powered by a black hole already 360 million times the sun's mass — and feeding slowly. Either it grew in furious early bursts, or it was born big. The models have a problem.

item.title: A Chatbot Designed Proteins. About One in Nine Actually Stuck to Their Targets.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: OpenAI says its GPT-6 models can sketch new protein shapes and sequences with nothing but reasoning and code, and that 35 of 322 lab-tested designs bound their targets. Specialist tools still did key steps, and some scientists suspect memorization.

item.title: A Leaky Truck Painted Three States Purple. Nobody Is Cleaning It Up.
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: A vivid purple streak ran for miles along highways in New Jersey, New York, and into Pennsylvania. Officials traced it to a leaking tractor-trailer hauling car wash dye. The substance is non-hazardous, so the official cleanup plan is: rain.

item.title: GTA 6 Emptied Call of Duty. Four Days Later, It Still Hasn't Filled Back Up.
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Alinea Analytics estimates Call of Duty's daily players fell 42% on GTA 6's launch day and were still 41% below baseline four days later — the slowest recovery of the big live-service games, despite the least audience overlap. These are analyst estimates, not official counts. The behavior they describe is the story.

item.title: Metal Dust in Dirty Air Flips a Switch in Your Airways. Scientists Say Existing Drugs Can Flip It Back.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: A King's College London and Cardiff University study links metal particles in air pollution to severe asthma attacks and names the airway sensor they trigger. Drugs that block it worked in lab tests, not yet in patients.

item.title: Police Saw Benjamin Franklin on Hanover Street. They Recognized a Man With Two Warrants.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: A 66-year-old Boston tour guide who works as a Franklin impersonator was arrested in full colonial costume in the North End — and showed up to his arraignment still wearing it.

item.title: Teletubbies Are Moving to Netflix. Britain's TV-Tax-Funded Kids' Channel Is Following the Children.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: The BBC will put shows from 24 CBeebies programs, including Hey Duggee and Numberblocks, in a branded Netflix hub from December 2. A separate deal brings the shows to U.S. Netflix.

item.title: The Same Charge Jack Smith Used on Trump Is Now Being Waved at Democrats. No One Has Been Charged.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: A Texas U.S. attorney and the White House counsel have warned incoming Democratic investigators that their oversight could amount to a federal "conspiracy against rights." Legal experts call it payback; the Justice Department says it is enforcing the law.

item.title: The Witcher 4 Just Signed With PlayStation. CD Projekt Says Expect a GTA VI-Sized Leap.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: On its third-quarter earnings call, CD Projekt Red said it signed new agreements with Sony covering PlayStation, PlayStation Plus and the coming Witcher 4 marketing campaign. The game is still due in 2028.

item.title: Tidal Is Deleting the Robots: 29 Million AI Songs Headed for Removal
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Tidal says more than 43% of tracks uploaded in the last 90 days were fully AI-generated. Starting December 9, it will ban and remove them — a private platform cleaning its own house, no government ban required.

item.title: Two Brothers Bought a Century-Old Diner Off Facebook Marketplace. Now They Want Another Hundred Years.
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Dumont Brothers Diner in Dumont, New Jersey, opened November 9 in the old Dumont Crystal Diner, billed as Bergen County's oldest. Gus and John Grimanis kept the memorabilia, added Greek family recipes, and drew hundreds to the grand opening. Plus: the Belmont Café in Waymart is back in business.

item.title: The President Picked the CEO. The Board Said Yes. Congress Wants to Know Who Else Was in the Room.
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Eleven days after Jensen Huang resigned over an affair with a woman U.S. authorities suspect of spying for China, Nvidia's board brought him back — after the president lobbied the board himself. The stock gained $900 billion in a day. Congress, from both parties, is not satisfied.
